forest.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Reduce n signed int32 integers to one exact int32 sum. Values are bounded to [-5,5], so the true sum fits int32. Performance n=4194304 (2^22); checks include n=1,127,1024,65536 and performance n. input1=x; input2,input3 ignored. output has one int32; scratch contains 2*n+65536 int32 values. Complete the entire reduction on device, not only the first stage.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.

Intégrer de Gm1 uniquement la réduction directe pour 2 ≤ n ≤ 128, en conservant le chemin n=1, le chemin atomique grande taille de f24 et son fallback pour les autres tailles. Gm1 est correct mais plus lent (7,335 µs) car son chemin grande taille est différent; l’intégration doit donc préserver f24 à n=4194304. Mesurer la combinaison et vérifier tous les cas avant de la retenir.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore large-input hierarchical reduction for n=4194304. Replace the current modulo-based interleaved reduction and repeated block-wide synchronization with an efficient warp/block reduction approach, while having CTAs accumulate multiple values per thread from coalesced, disjoint input tiles. Write partials to bounded scratch and reduce them directly to out. Tune tile and block configuration; compare a two-stage path with an additional final reduction stage if the partial count makes a single final CTA inefficient. Cover all legal sizes with bounded reads, exact int32 output, unchanged ABI/default stream, and a correct fallback. Compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline.
children.subject: Large-input hierarchical reduction and warp/block reduction costs

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a generic size-based single-CTA reduction that writes directly to out for small inputs, eliminating intermediate partials and the final device copy where beneficial. Measure crossover thresholds rather than hardcoding test sizes. Explicitly compare against the baseline n=1 device-to-device copy path, which launches no kernel, and retain whichever path measures better. Keep a correct fallback for larger inputs and preserve correctness, bounded reads, exact int32 results, ABI, and default-stream behavior for every legal size. Compare all checks and repeated timings.
children.subject: Small-input direct-output reduction and launch crossover

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, evaluate a large-input alternative with an ordered output-zeroing kernel followed by a multi-CTA grid-stride reduction; each CTA reduces its own values and performs one int32 atomicAdd to out. Tune CTA count/work per CTA to balance input throughput against contention. Do not rely on initialized scratch or unsafe inter-block initialization. Preserve exact results, bounds, ABI, default-stream ordering, and a correct fallback for other legal sizes; compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline and hierarchical approach.
children.subject: Large-input atomic final aggregation

data.analysis: Keep N=3 and all role identities. T1 currently prescribes two stages without guarding against an oversized or slow final CTA; the source also has an unused warp-reduction helper while reduce0 uses modulo-based interleaving and repeated block synchronization. Refine T1 to test those reduction costs and permit another final stage if measurements warrant it. T2 should not assume a kernel beats the baseline n=1 device copy, which launches no kernel. T3 remains a useful contrast to T1: explicit output initialization plus one atomic per CTA instead of scratch partials. No extra tree is justified.

data.shared_assumptions: Target: one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3; preserve the run signature, default stream, one-int output, and device-only computation. Scratch is uninitialized and limited to 2*n+65536 int32 values; add no allocations or devices. Use input1 only and compute from every current input. Supplied checks include n=1,127,1024,65536 and performance n=4194304. The supplied baseline is valid and averages 46.67 µs over three samples; its large-n source path launches four reduction kernels and then copies the result to out. That source structure does not measure the contribution of each cost. Compare candidate measurements under the fixed harness and confirm the eventual integration.
